manufacturer: Mecke Reagent (selenious acid + H2SO4) — Standard forensic spot test
validationStatus: Prototype — colour regions from UNODC ST/NAR/42 (2013) Table 4 and Mecke (1899) Pharm Zentralhalle. Differentiates opiates (blue-green/black), MDMA (blue-green), ketamine (orange-yellow). Not a validated diagnostic instrument.

referenceCard.description: Software-rendered 8-patch digital reference card displayed on-screen.
referenceCard.printNotes: No printing required. Display on a second device beside the sample.

reactionWindow.observationNotes: Mecke reaction is fast — most colour change occurs within 30 seconds. Capture when colour has stabilised.

captureInstructions: Add 1-2 drops of Mecke reagent to a small sample on a white ceramic surface.
Observe colour change within 30-60 seconds: blue-green/black = opiates, blue-green = MDMA, orange = ketamine.
Display the Digital Reference Card on a second device beside the sample.
Frame both the reaction area and the digital card within their guides.
Press CHECK FRAME until the guard accepts, then press CAPTURE.
safetyNotes: Mecke reagent contains selenious acid and concentrated sulfuric acid. Selenium compounds are highly toxic.
Wear nitrile gloves, safety goggles, and a lab coat. Work in a fume hood.
Selenium waste requires specialist disposal — do not pour down drains.
Black/dark blue = opiates. Blue-green = MDMA/MDA. Orange-yellow = ketamine. Results are presumptive only.
Confirmatory laboratory analysis is mandatory before any legal proceedings under NDPS Act.
